section_1.title: The Putnam Mindset: Beyond Standard Algorithms
section_1.content: Introduction to the Putnam philosophy: Problems aren't about brute force, but 'mathematical elegance.' We define the transition from high-school procedural math to competition-level logical synthesis.
section_1.example: Visualize a squirrel trying to crack a nut: Standard math uses a hammer; Putnam math analyzes the nut's structural stress points to find the single hairline fracture.

section_2.title: Core Strategy: Invariant Analysis
section_2.content: Introduce 'Invariants'—quantities or properties that remain unchanged under a system's transformation. Prerequisite: Basic modular arithmetic and parity concepts. Graphical representation: A flow chart showing a dynamic state machine where one specific value remains constant.
section_2.example: A room full of chameleons changing colors. By tracking the parity of color counts (the invariant), we prove whether they can ever all become the same color.

section_3.title: Tactical Tool: The Pigeonhole Principle & Extremal Thinking
section_3.content: How to handle existence proofs. We focus on the 'Extremal Principle'—examining the smallest or largest configuration to force a contradiction or discovery.
section_3.example: A robotic arm placing sensors on a grid. We use the 'Pigeonhole Principle' to show that if you have N+1 sensors and N spots, at least one spot must have two sensors, triggering a logic circuit.

section_4.title: Integration: Bridging Calculus and Combinatorics
section_4.content: Putnam problems often bridge disparate fields. We demonstrate how to apply Integral Bounds to solve discrete counting problems, visualised as area under a curve representing discrete bars.
section_4.example: Using the 'Riemann Sum' approximation to bound the number of paths a robot can take through a maze, turning a complex summation into a smooth geometric integral.

section_5.title: Synthesis: The Final Countdown
section_5.content: Summary of the 3-step workflow: 1. Identify the invariant, 2. Test the extreme case, 3. Connect the abstract result back to the original constraint. Encouragement to seek beauty in the proof.
section_5.example: The 'Archimedes' moment: A final animation showing all disconnected strategy pieces clicking together like a complex clockwork mechanism to solve a classic 1990s Putnam challenge.
